_meta.note: SECOND domain provider — proves the adapter architecture generalizes beyond code. The docs/research adapter (plugin/adapters/docs/) reads a markdown CITATION graph (a section that links to another 'builds on' it) into the SAME codemap contract, so the UNCHANGED code-adapter engine (deplint.js) and the generic context hook work on it with zero changes — only the *-map.js provider is new. In a docs project the section IS the unit of work (one authoring task per section), so docs-map emits the FULL codemap — both edges AND tasks (task id = section basename, mapping to [that section]) — i.e. the whole contract is provider-produced, not hand-authored (unlike code, where task->symbol is genuinely fuzzy). Seam 1 (plan authoring): deplint catches MISSING (drafting a citing section before the cited one), REDUNDANT, COLLISION on a docs authoring DAG. Seam 2 (context assembly): docs-context.js injects the CITED sections' TEXT into a task's context via the generic context_cmd hook (already parity-proven, T89). BOUNDARY (same as code): node-only, not scaffolded, not a parity surface, imports nothing from core; suites green without it. Ollama (llama3.2:3b etc. local) drives a harness-first/on-demand Seam-2 demo (not gated). Spec-first; adversarial review on both gates. Continues the code-adapter branch (reuses deplint.js + the context hook shipped there).

phases.title: Docs citation provider — the same engine, a new domain (Seam 1)

tasks.title: Author the docs Seam-1 proof + fixture corpus (spec-first)
tasks.description: Spec-first: write docs/howto/gate-examples/docs-deplint.sh — a proof that MUST fail before docs-map.js exists. Author a fixture markdown corpus under plugin/adapters/docs/fixtures/corpus/: background.md (# Background, no links), method.md (# Method, links to [background](background.md) AND an external [ref](https://example.com)), results.md (# Results, links to [method](method.md)), intro.md (# Intro, links to [background](background.md) and [method](method.md)). Task id = section basename (one authoring task per section). Author plugin/adapters/docs/fixtures/docs.codemap.json = the FULL expected docs-map output: { edges:[["method","background"],["results","method"],["intro","background"],["intro","method"]], tasks:{"background":["background"],"method":["method"],"results":["results"],"intro":["intro"]} } (edge = citer depends on cited). Also docs-unordered.dag.json (tasks background,method,results,intro all requires []) and docs-clean.dag.json (background:[], method:[background], intro:[background,method], results:[method]). The proof asserts: (1) `node plugin/adapters/docs/docs-map.js <corpus>` emits BOTH edges AND tasks equal to docs.codemap.json — edges INCLUDE the four citation pairs and EXCLUDE the external https link and any self-link, and tasks map each section to itself (order-insensitive set-equality on BOTH, so an edges-only or echo mapper fails); (2) THE UNCHANGED code engine generalizes: `node plugin/adapters/code/deplint.js docs-unordered.dag.json docs.codemap.json` reports missing>=1 AND the CORRECTLY-DIRECTED suggestion — it MUST print the exact line 'method should require background' (the citing-section task requires the cited-section task) and MUST NOT print the reverse 'background should require method'; and `... docs-clean.dag.json ...` reports missing=0. set -euo pipefail + explicit exits. Marker DOCS-DEPLINT-OK; fails before docs-map.js exists. Fast (<5s).

tasks.title: Implement docs-map.js (markdown citation graph -> full codemap)
tasks.description: Create plugin/adapters/docs/docs-map.js: a pure module citationMap(corpusDir) -> { edges: [[citerId, citedId], ...], tasks: { <sectionId>: [<sectionId>], ... } }. Scan *.md in the corpus dir; unit id = basename without .md. Parse markdown links; keep ONLY relative links that resolve to another .md file IN the corpus (drop http(s)://, mailto:, bare #anchors, and links outside the corpus); emit edge [thisId, targetId] meaning the citing section depends on the cited one; dedupe; no self-edges. ALSO emit tasks: one entry per section, `{ sectionId: [sectionId] }` — the docs convention that each authoring task produces one section — so the FULL codemap (edges + tasks) is provider-produced, not hand-authored. CLI `node docs-map.js <corpusDir>` prints the full codemap JSON. Pure Node stdlib only; imports nothing from core (boundary). Also write plugin/adapters/docs/README.md documenting: the citation->codemap mapping, the 1:1 section=task convention (and that a project using different task ids must supply its own tasks map), that the SAME deplint.js validates a docs authoring DAG (Seam 1) with no engine change, and the boundary (node-only, not scaffolded, not a parity surface).

tasks.title: Wire the docs Seam-1 proof (T90)

Keep the whole node suite green. Do NOT modify plugin/bootstrap.sh (the docs adapter must stay out of the .hb scaffold) and do NOT modify plugin/adapters/code/deplint.js (the point is the engine is UNCHANGED — the docs domain reuses it as-is).

tasks.title: Author the docs Seam-2 proof (spec-first)
tasks.description: Spec-first: write docs/howto/gate-examples/docs-context.sh — a proof that MUST fail before docs-context.js exists. Reuse the DP fixture corpus + docs.codemap.json. It asserts `node plugin/adapters/docs/docs-context.js plugin/adapters/docs/fixtures/corpus plugin/adapters/docs/fixtures/docs.codemap.json TD` (task TD authors 'results', which DIRECTLY cites 'method') emits the CITED section's TEXT: the output contains a distinctive line from method.md (e.g. '# Method'), and MUST NOT contain background.md's text (background is a 2-hop citation, not direct) nor results.md's own body (a section does not cite itself). This proves it renders the direct-citation subgraph's TEXT, not the whole corpus and not an echo. set -euo pipefail + explicit exits. Marker DOCS-CONTEXT-OK; fails before docs-context.js exists. Fast (<5s).

tasks.title: Implement docs-context.js + on-demand ollama demo
tasks.description: Create plugin/adapters/docs/docs-context.js: `node docs-context.js <corpusDir> <codemap.json> <taskId>` -> for the section(s) codemap.tasks[taskId] touches, find their DIRECT citations (edges from those sections in codemap.edges), and render each cited section's heading + text read from the corpus, as a readable 'read these before writing' block. Pure Node stdlib; imports nothing from core. This is the docs Seam-2 provider that plugs into the EXISTING generic context_cmd hook (no executor change — the hook is domain-neutral and already parity-proven by T89). Also add tests/real-docs-context.sh: an ON-DEMAND, harness-first demo that wires docs-context.js as the context_cmd for a real ollama model (HB_EXEC_MODEL=llama3.2:3b), drives one task, and shows the cited section text reached the prompt; skips cleanly without ollama; NOT wired into the suite.

GATE_DP.desc: The docs provider turns a markdown citation graph into the codemap contract (citer->cited edges, external/non-corpus links excluded), and the UNCHANGED code-adapter deplint.js validates a docs authoring DAG on it — catching a correctly-directed MISSING on an unordered plan and clearing an ordered one. Provider imports nothing from core; the engine is not forked.

review.prompt: Refute that DP is done. Does docs-map emit citer->cited edges from REAL markdown links and correctly EXCLUDE external (https) and non-corpus links (does the proof assert both an included pair AND the external link's absence, order-insensitively)? Does the proof genuinely prove the GENERALIZATION — running the UNCHANGED plugin/adapters/code/deplint.js on the DOCS codemap, catching a correctly-DIRECTED missing edge (citing-section task should require the cited-section task, not the reverse) on the unordered DAG and reporting clean on the ordered one? Could DOCS-DEPLINT-OK print vacuously (set -euo pipefail? explicit exits? fail-before-docs-map-exists)? Was deplint.js actually left UNCHANGED (the whole point — no code-engine edits)? Does docs-map import anything from core? Is the direction right: an edge [X,Y] means X (citer) depends on Y (cited)?
